reviews.literary_form_evidence: Lev.7.1-6 is a closed reparation-offering procedure, while Lev.7.7-10 is a complete cross-offering allocation digest linked to the purification, burnt, and grain offering manuals.
reviews.counterevidence: Lev.7.7 begins by comparing the reparation and purification offerings, so the digest remains tightly attached to the preceding procedure and is only four verses long.
reviews.remedy: Split into M7_sol-Lev-012a Lev.7.1-6 and M7_sol-Lev-012b Lev.7.7-10, preserving the existing typed links from 012b to decisions 011, 008, and 009.

reviews.literary_form_evidence: The eighth-day summons and commands open one command-execution-result narrative that closes with Aaron's blessing, Yahweh's appearing glory, consuming fire, and the congregation's response.
reviews.counterevidence: Seams at Lev.9.5, 9.8, 9.15, and 9.22 distinguish preparation, Aaron's offering, the people's offering, and the climactic blessing.
reviews.remedy: Retain Lev.9.1-24 as one chunk and preserve its relation to the surrounding ordination and unauthorized-fire sequence.

reviews.literary_form_evidence: The appointed-times heading introduces a complete weekly-Sabbath provision that closes before the repeated annual-calendar heading at Lev.23.4.
reviews.counterevidence: Because Lev.23.1-2 may govern the whole chapter, this three-verse child risks detaching the global heading and producing a small retrieval unit.
reviews.remedy: Retain the child under the mandatory Lev.23.1-44 calendar parent and expose its heading-to-Sabbath function; it is complete despite its size.

reviews.literary_form_evidence: The renewed appointed-times heading opens the dated annual sequence and the linked Passover-Unleavened-Bread observance closes before a fresh speech at Lev.23.9.
reviews.counterevidence: Passover at Lev.23.5 and Unleavened Bread at Lev.23.6-8 are distinguishable observances, while Lev.23.4 may merely resume the chapter-wide heading.
reviews.remedy: Retain Lev.23.4-8 as one child under the Lev.23.1-44 calendar parent.

reviews.literary_form_evidence: A complete divine-speech frame supplies date, memorial observance, holy convocation, work prohibition, and offering requirement before the fresh speech at Lev.23.26.
reviews.counterevidence: The three-verse unit is small and shares seventh-month placement and rest language with the following Day of Atonement observance.
reviews.remedy: Retain this complete child under both the Lev.23.1-44 calendar parent and the Lev.23.23-32 seventh-month sibling relation.

reviews.literary_form_evidence: A fresh speech changes the date and observance, develops self-affliction and sanctions, and closes with explicit evening-to-evening Sabbath bounds.
reviews.counterevidence: Its seventh-month sequence and Sabbath vocabulary closely connect it to Lev.23.23-25, while its ritual meaning depends on the larger Lev.16 atonement procedure.
reviews.remedy: Retain Lev.23.26-32 with explicit relations to Lev.23.23-25 and Lev.16.29-34.

reviews.literary_form_evidence: The offense and custody generate a divine ruling expanded into generalized and equal-law provisions, and the execution closes the complete case-ruling-performance frame.
reviews.counterevidence: Lev.24.10-12, 24.13-22, and 24.23 could function separately as narrative problem, legal ruling, and execution.
reviews.remedy: Retain Lev.24.10-23 as one narrative-legal unit, with the internal problem-ruling-execution sequence visible in metadata.

reviews.literary_form_evidence: Lev.26.1-2 is a compact allegiance frame closed by divine self-identification, whereas the conditional blessing discourse formally opens at Lev.26.3 and closes with the exodus-freedom affirmation at Lev.26.13.
reviews.counterevidence: The allegiance commands naturally establish the obedience presupposed by the blessings, and splitting them creates a two-verse child inside one uninterrupted Mount Sinai speech.
reviews.remedy: Split into M7_sol-Lev-061a Lev.26.1-2 and M7_sol-Lev-061b Lev.26.3-13, retain both under the Lev.25.1-26.46 speech parent, and keep the split candidate-held for final adjudication.
